questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which statement best describes cloud computing
questions.question: Which statement best describes cloud computing?
options: Using computing resources delivered over a network on demand, usually with usage-based pricing
Buying a physical server for every application
Using only software installed on a personal laptop
Storing every file on a USB drive
questions.correct_answer: Using computing resources delivered over a network on demand, usually with usage-based pricing
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides on-demand access to shared computing resources such as servers, storage and networking. Ownership of physical hardware is not required.

distractor_feedback.Buying a physical server for every appli: Buying hardware is traditional on-premises provisioning, not the defining feature of cloud computing.
distractor_feedback.Using only software installed on a perso: Local software can be used without cloud infrastructure.
distractor_feedback.Storing every file on a USB drive: A USB drive is local storage, not an on-demand cloud service.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: A team needs virtual machines but wants to manage the operating system and installed softw
questions.question: A team needs virtual machines but wants to manage the operating system and installed software. Which service model fits best?
questions.correct_answer: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
questions.explanation: IaaS supplies fundamental infrastructure such as virtual machines, storage and networks while the customer manages the guest OS and applications.

distractor_feedback.A finished business application: A finished application is closer to SaaS than IaaS.
distractor_feedback.Software as a Service (SaaS): SaaS gives the customer a finished application and much less infrastructure control.
distractor_feedback.Function as a Service (FaaS): FaaS runs event-triggered functions rather than giving general-purpose VM administration.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which is the clearest example of SaaS
questions.question: Which is the clearest example of SaaS?
options: Installing a hypervisor on a physical server
Using a browser-based email application managed by its provider
Creating and patching your own virtual machine
questions.correct_answer: Using a browser-based email application managed by its provider
questions.explanation: With SaaS, the provider operates the application and underlying platform; the customer mainly uses and configures the service.

distractor_feedback.Configuring a VPC route table: A route table is a networking resource, not an end-user application.
distractor_feedback.Installing a hypervisor on a physical se: Installing a hypervisor is infrastructure management.
distractor_feedback.Creating and patching your own virtual m: Creating and patching a VM is infrastructure administration.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is a key characteristic of a public cloud
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of a public cloud?
options: Every customer owns a separate physical data centre
Resources can only be accessed from one office
The customer must maintain all provider hardware
A provider makes computing services available to multiple customers over the internet or private connectivity
questions.correct_answer: A provider makes computing services available to multiple customers over the internet or private connectivity
questions.explanation: Public cloud services are offered by a cloud provider to many customers, with logical isolation between customer environments.

distractor_feedback.Every customer owns a separate physical: Customers generally do not each own a separate provider data centre.
distractor_feedback.Resources can only be accessed from one: Access is not inherently restricted to one office.
distractor_feedback.The customer must maintain all provider: The provider maintains the underlying cloud hardware.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: An organisation uses its own data centre for sensitive workloads and a public cloud for va
questions.question: An organisation uses its own data centre for sensitive workloads and a public cloud for variable demand. What deployment approach is this?
questions.correct_answer: Hybrid cloud
questions.explanation: A hybrid approach combines private infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing workloads or data to span the environments.

distractor_feedback.Public cloud only: Public-only does not include the organisation's private data centre.
distractor_feedback.Private cloud only: Private-only does not include public cloud services.
distractor_feedback.Community cloud only: Community cloud is shared by organisations with common requirements, not simply private plus public.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does elasticity mean in cloud computing
questions.question: What does elasticity mean in cloud computing?
options: Resources can expand or contract to match changing demand
Every resource must remain at a fixed size
A server is physically moved between data centres
questions.correct_answer: Resources can expand or contract to match changing demand
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability to adjust resource capacity in response to workload demand.

distractor_feedback.All workloads must run continuously: Elasticity does not require every workload to run continuously.
distractor_feedback.Every resource must remain at a fixed si: Fixed capacity is the opposite of elasticity.
distractor_feedback.A server is physically moved between dat: Physical relocation is not the definition.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which benefit is most directly associated with measured, usage-based cloud billing
questions.question: Which benefit is most directly associated with measured, usage-based cloud billing?
options: Costs never change from month to month
The provider transfers ownership of hardware to the customer
Paying for the resources consumed rather than purchasing all capacity upfront
questions.correct_answer: Paying for the resources consumed rather than purchasing all capacity upfront
questions.explanation: Measured service makes usage observable and supports consumption-based billing; costs still need monitoring.

distractor_feedback.Costs never change from month to month: Usage changes can make bills vary.
distractor_feedback.The provider transfers ownership of hard: Customers normally consume provider-owned infrastructure rather than receiving its ownership.
distractor_feedback.All cloud services are free: Cloud services are not universally free.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: In a shared-responsibility model, who is generally responsible for securing the physical d
questions.question: In a shared-responsibility model, who is generally responsible for securing the physical data centre?
questions.correct_answer: The cloud provider
questions.explanation: The provider is responsible for security of the cloud, including physical facilities and underlying infrastructure.

distractor_feedback.The customer using the service: Customers remain responsible for many controls in the cloud, but not the provider's physical facility.
distractor_feedback.The customer's application end users: End users do not operate the cloud provider's data centre.
distractor_feedback.The customer's Git repository: A Git repository does not own or secure the facility.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which task is commonly the customer's responsibility when running an IaaS virtual machine
questions.question: Which task is commonly the customer's responsibility when running an IaaS virtual machine?
options: Patching and securing the guest operating system
Replacing failed disks in the provider's storage array
questions.correct_answer: Patching and securing the guest operating system
questions.explanation: With IaaS, customers typically manage the guest OS, applications, identities and configuration, while the provider manages physical infrastructure.

distractor_feedback.Replacing failed disks in the provider's: Physical storage hardware is provider responsibility.
distractor_feedback.Securing the provider's hypervisor hardw: The underlying virtualization infrastructure is provider responsibility.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is the main purpose of the SDLC
questions.question: What is the main purpose of the SDLC?
options: To guarantee that software never needs maintenance
To provide a structured process for planning, building, testing, releasing and maintaining software
To define only how servers are purchased
questions.correct_answer: To provide a structured process for planning, building, testing, releasing and maintaining software
questions.explanation: The Software Development Life Cycle structures software work from requirements through maintenance.

distractor_feedback.To guarantee that software never needs m: Software maintenance remains necessary after release.
distractor_feedback.To define only how servers are purchased: Server purchasing is only one possible operational concern.
distractor_feedback.To replace all software testing: Testing is an important SDLC activity, not something the SDLC replaces.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: A developer changes code, tests it, and releases it to users. Which SDLC phase most direct
questions.question: A developer changes code, tests it, and releases it to users. Which SDLC phase most directly describes making the change available to users?
questions.correct_answer: Deployment
questions.explanation: Deployment is the release or installation of a software change into its target environment.

distractor_feedback.Design: Design plans the solution before implementation.
distractor_feedback.Maintenance: Maintenance covers ongoing support and updates after release.
distractor_feedback.Requirements gathering: Requirements gathering identifies what should be built.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Why do teams separate development, testing and production environments
questions.question: Why do teams separate development, testing and production environments?
options: To make every environment behave differently
To validate changes before exposing real users and production data to them
questions.correct_answer: To validate changes before exposing real users and production data to them
questions.explanation: Separate environments reduce the risk of untested changes affecting production and allow controlled validation.

distractor_feedback.To avoid writing tests: Separate environments do not remove the need for tests.
distractor_feedback.To make every environment behave differe: The goal is controlled similarity, not arbitrary differences.
distractor_feedback.To ensure developers cannot collaborate: Environment separation does not prevent collaboration.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which statement about cloud scalability is accurate
questions.question: Which statement about cloud scalability is accurate?
options: A system can be designed to handle increased workload by adding resources or distributing work
Scalability means a system can never fail
Scalability always means buying a larger physical server
Scalability removes the need for monitoring
questions.correct_answer: A system can be designed to handle increased workload by adding resources or distributing work
questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to accommodate increased load, either vertically or horizontally.

distractor_feedback.Scalability always means buying a larger: Vertical scaling is only one approach; horizontal scaling adds instances or nodes.
distractor_feedback.Scalability removes the need for monitor: Monitoring remains important to understand demand and failures.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: A company wants to avoid buying enough servers for its rare peak traffic. Which cloud prop
questions.question: A company wants to avoid buying enough servers for its rare peak traffic. Which cloud property helps most?
questions.correct_answer: On-demand provisioning and elasticity
questions.explanation: On-demand provisioning and elasticity let the company add capacity when needed instead of permanently owning peak capacity.

distractor_feedback.Removing all access controls: Access controls are unrelated to capacity planning.
distractor_feedback.Manual hardware procurement: Manual procurement is slower and requires upfront purchasing.
distractor_feedback.Fixed-capacity planning only: Fixed capacity does not adapt to rare peaks.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is vendor lock-in
questions.question: What is vendor lock-in?
options: A virtual machine that is stopped
A cloud bill that is paid monthly
A situation where moving away from a provider is difficult or costly because of dependencies
A security group rule that blocks SSH
questions.correct_answer: A situation where moving away from a provider is difficult or costly because of dependencies
questions.explanation: Vendor lock-in can arise from proprietary services, data formats, skills or architectures that make migration difficult.

distractor_feedback.A virtual machine that is stopped: A stopped VM is a resource state.
distractor_feedback.A cloud bill that is paid monthly: Monthly billing is not vendor lock-in.
distractor_feedback.A security group rule that blocks SSH: A security group rule is a network access control.

questions.section: M1 Week 1 — Cloud Computing Fundamentals
questions.topic: Why should a cloud engineer monitor cloud spending
questions.question: Why should a cloud engineer monitor cloud spending?
options: Because monitoring automatically makes every service free
Because all resources stop billing when unused
To detect unexpected usage and keep resource costs within budget
questions.correct_answer: To detect unexpected usage and keep resource costs within budget
questions.explanation: Monitoring usage and cost helps identify waste, unexpected growth and budget risks.

distractor_feedback.Because monitoring automatically makes e: Monitoring does not make services free.
distractor_feedback.Because all resources stop billing when: Some stopped resources, such as attached storage, can still incur charges.
distractor_feedback.Because cloud pricing never changes: Cloud pricing and usage can change.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is the primary role of an operating system
questions.question: What is the primary role of an operating system?
options: To manage hardware resources and provide services for applications and users
To act only as a text editor
To provide internet access without networking hardware
questions.correct_answer: To manage hardware resources and provide services for applications and users
questions.explanation: An OS manages resources such as CPU, memory, storage and devices, and provides an environment for programs.

distractor_feedback.To act only as a text editor: A text editor is an application, not the OS's primary role.
distractor_feedback.To replace the computer's CPU: The OS manages the CPU; it does not replace it.
distractor_feedback.To provide internet access without netwo: Internet access also depends on networking hardware and connectivity.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is the Linux kernel
questions.question: What is the Linux kernel?
options: The core of the operating system that manages hardware and system resources
questions.correct_answer: The core of the operating system that manages hardware and system resources
questions.explanation: The kernel handles core functions such as process scheduling, memory management and device interaction.

distractor_feedback.A package manager: A package manager installs and manages software.
distractor_feedback.A user-created shell script: A shell script is a user-level program.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which command prints the current working directory
questions.question: Which command prints the current working directory?
questions.correct_answer: pwd
questions.explanation: `pwd` prints the absolute path of the current working directory.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: You want to list files, including hidden dotfiles, in long format. Which command is approp
questions.question: You want to list files, including hidden dotfiles, in long format. Which command is appropriate?
questions.correct_answer: ls -la
questions.explanation: `ls -l` requests long format and `-a` includes hidden entries whose names begin with a dot.

distractor_feedback.pwd -la: `pwd` prints a path and does not list directory entries.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which command changes the current directory to /var/log
questions.question: Which command changes the current directory to /var/log?
questions.correct_answer: cd /var/log
questions.explanation: `cd` changes the shell's current working directory.

distractor_feedback.pwd /var/log: `pwd` displays the current path; it does not change it.
distractor_feedback.touch /var/log: `touch` creates an empty file or updates timestamps.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does `mkdir -p project/logs` do
questions.question: What does `mkdir -p project/logs` do?
options: Creates the directory path, including missing parent directories
questions.correct_answer: Creates the directory path, including missing parent directories
questions.explanation: The `-p` option creates missing parent directories and does not complain if the target directory already exists.

distractor_feedback.Lists the directory tree: Listing requires a command such as `ls`.
distractor_feedback.Deletes project and logs: The command does not delete directories.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which command displays the contents of a text file in the terminal
questions.question: Which command displays the contents of a text file in the terminal?
questions.correct_answer: cat notes.txt
questions.explanation: `cat` outputs file contents to standard output.

distractor_feedback.cd notes.txt: `cd` changes directories and expects a directory path.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does `cp source.txt backup.txt` do
questions.question: What does `cp source.txt backup.txt` do?
options: Moves source.txt and removes the original
questions.correct_answer: Copies source.txt to backup.txt
questions.explanation: `cp` copies the source file to the destination path.

distractor_feedback.Renames the current directory: The command acts on files, not the current directory name.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which command moves a file or renames it
questions.question: Which command moves a file or renames it?
questions.correct_answer: mv old.txt new.txt
questions.explanation: `mv` moves a file or renames it when source and destination are in the same directory.

distractor_feedback.cp old.txt new.txt: `cp` creates a copy and leaves the original.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does `rm -r old-folder` do
questions.question: What does `rm -r old-folder` do?
options: Moves the directory to the home folder
Removes a directory and its contents recursively
Displays all files in the directory
questions.correct_answer: Removes a directory and its contents recursively
questions.explanation: The recursive option allows `rm` to remove directories and their contents; use it carefully.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: In Linux permissions, what does `r` represent
questions.question: In Linux permissions, what does `r` represent?
questions.correct_answer: Read permission
questions.explanation: The `r` permission allows reading a file or, for directories, listing entries subject to other permissions.

distractor_feedback.Rename permission: There is no standard rename permission bit.
distractor_feedback.Remote access: Remote access is unrelated to this permission symbol.
distractor_feedback.Run as root: Root privilege is not represented by `r`.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: For a directory, what does execute (`x`) permission allow
questions.question: For a directory, what does execute (`x`) permission allow?
options: Traversing or entering the directory when path permissions permit
questions.correct_answer: Traversing or entering the directory when path permissions permit
questions.explanation: Directory execute permission allows traversal/search of the directory; read permission controls listing names.

distractor_feedback.Editing every file inside it: Editing files depends on file permissions and directory write permissions.
distractor_feedback.Changing its owner: Ownership changes require suitable privileges and `chown`.
distractor_feedback.Automatically granting root access: Execute permission does not grant root access.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does `chmod 755 script.sh` set
questions.question: What does `chmod 755 script.sh` set?
options: Owner: read/write/execute; group and others: read/execute
Owner: read only; others: no access
Owner: read/write; group: write; others: execute only
questions.correct_answer: Owner: read/write/execute; group and others: read/execute
questions.explanation: In octal permissions, 7 is rwx and 5 is r-x, so 755 means owner rwx and group/others r-x.

distractor_feedback.Owner: read/write; group: write; others:: The stated combination does not correspond to 755.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: Which command shows running processes
questions.question: Which command shows running processes?
questions.correct_answer: ps
questions.explanation: `ps` reports process information; options such as `ps aux` show a broader process listing on common Linux systems.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What is a zombie process
questions.question: What is a zombie process?
options: A process that has no parent and is always running
A malicious program that hides its name
A process that has finished but still has an entry awaiting collection by its parent
questions.correct_answer: A process that has finished but still has an entry awaiting collection by its parent
questions.explanation: A zombie has terminated, but its parent has not yet collected its exit status with a wait operation.

distractor_feedback.A process that has no parent and is alwa: An orphan is a running process whose parent has exited; it is not the definition of zombie.
distractor_feedback.A malicious program that hides its name: A hidden malicious process is unrelated.
distractor_feedback.A process using 100% CPU forever: High CPU use describes a running process, not a zombie.

questions.section: M1 Week 2 — Linux Fundamentals
questions.topic: What does `sudo apt update` do on Ubuntu/Debian systems
questions.question: What does `sudo apt update` do on Ubuntu/Debian systems?
options: Deletes cached packages and user files
Installs the Linux kernel from source
Refreshes the local package index from configured repositories
questions.correct_answer: Refreshes the local package index from configured repositories
questions.explanation: `apt update` downloads updated package metadata; package upgrades are a separate operation such as `apt upgrade`.

distractor_feedback.Deletes cached packages and user files: The command does not delete user files.
distractor_feedback.Installs the Linux kernel from source: It does not compile and install a kernel from source.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What problem does version control solve
questions.question: What problem does version control solve?
options: It records changes over time so work can be reviewed, compared and restored
It automatically prevents every coding error
It replaces the need for backups in all situations
questions.correct_answer: It records changes over time so work can be reviewed, compared and restored
questions.explanation: Version control tracks project history and supports collaboration, branching and recovery of earlier states.

distractor_feedback.It automatically prevents every coding e: Version control cannot prevent every bug.
distractor_feedback.It replaces the need for backups in all: A Git repository is not a complete backup strategy by itself.
distractor_feedback.It hosts websites by itself: Git tracks files; it does not itself host a website.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is Git
questions.question: What is Git?
questions.correct_answer: A distributed version control system
questions.explanation: Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in files.

distractor_feedback.A cloud provider: A cloud provider offers infrastructure and services.
distractor_feedback.A programming language: Git is not a programming language.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is GitHub primarily used for
questions.question: What is GitHub primarily used for?
options: Automatically deploying every repository to production
Hosting Git repositories and providing collaboration tools
questions.correct_answer: Hosting Git repositories and providing collaboration tools
questions.explanation: GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration features such as pull requests and issue tracking.

distractor_feedback.Managing Linux users: Linux users are managed by the operating system.
distractor_feedback.Automatically deploying every repository: Deployment requires configuration and is not automatic for every repository.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: Which command initializes a Git repository in the current directory
questions.question: Which command initializes a Git repository in the current directory?
questions.correct_answer: git init
questions.explanation: `git init` creates a new local Git repository in the current directory.

distractor_feedback.git start: `git start` is not the standard Git command for initialization.
distractor_feedback.git push: `git push` sends local commits to a remote.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is the staging area used for
questions.question: What is the staging area used for?
options: Selecting changes that will be included in the next commit
questions.correct_answer: Selecting changes that will be included in the next commit
questions.explanation: The staging area lets you choose which changes form the next commit.

distractor_feedback.Storing files permanently on GitHub: A commit is local until pushed; staging is not GitHub storage.
distractor_feedback.Running automated tests: Testing is performed by test tools or scripts.
distractor_feedback.Creating a new remote repository: Creating a remote repository is a hosting-platform action.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: Which command stages all changes in the current directory tree
questions.question: Which command stages all changes in the current directory tree?
questions.correct_answer: git add .
questions.explanation: `git add .` stages new, modified and deleted changes under the current directory, subject to ignore rules.

`git commit` records staged changes; it does not stage them by itself.
`git push` sends commits to a remote.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What does `git commit -m "Fix login bug"` do
questions.question: What does `git commit -m "Fix login bug"` do?
options: Creates a commit from staged changes with the supplied message
questions.correct_answer: Creates a commit from staged changes with the supplied message
questions.explanation: A commit records the staged snapshot in the local repository history.

distractor_feedback.Creates a new branch: Creating a branch uses `git branch` or `git switch -c`.
distractor_feedback.Downloads changes from a remote: Downloading remote updates uses `git fetch` or `git pull`.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: Why should a commit message be meaningful
questions.question: Why should a commit message be meaningful?
options: It helps people understand the purpose of a change in project history
questions.correct_answer: It helps people understand the purpose of a change in project history
questions.explanation: A useful commit message makes history easier to understand and review.

distractor_feedback.It determines the file permissions: Permissions are controlled by filesystem or Git mode changes.
distractor_feedback.It encrypts the commit: Commit messages do not encrypt commits.
distractor_feedback.It replaces the code review: A message does not replace code review.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is a branch in Git
questions.question: What is a branch in Git?
options: An independent line of development within a repository
A copy of GitHub's entire internet service
questions.correct_answer: An independent line of development within a repository
questions.explanation: Branches allow work on features or fixes without immediately changing another branch's history.

distractor_feedback.A separate physical server: A branch is a reference in repository history, not a server.
distractor_feedback.A copy of GitHub's entire internet servi: It does not copy GitHub's service.
distractor_feedback.A file permission setting: It is unrelated to filesystem permissions.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: Which command creates and switches to a new branch named feature-a
questions.question: Which command creates and switches to a new branch named feature-a?
questions.correct_answer: git switch -c feature-a
questions.explanation: `git switch -c` creates a branch and checks it out.

distractor_feedback.git fetch -c feature-a: `git fetch` downloads remote references and does not create/check out a local branch this way.
distractor_feedback.git push feature-a: `git push` sends commits to a remote branch.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What does `git clone URL` do
questions.question: What does `git clone URL` do?
options: Only downloads the latest single file
Creates a local copy of a remote repository, including its history
Uploads the current folder to the remote
questions.correct_answer: Creates a local copy of a remote repository, including its history
questions.explanation: Cloning creates a local repository and configures the source remote, usually named origin.

distractor_feedback.Deletes the remote repository: Cloning does not delete the source.
distractor_feedback.Only downloads the latest single file: A clone includes repository history, not just one file.
distractor_feedback.Uploads the current folder to the remote: Uploading changes is done with push.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What does `git fetch` do
questions.question: What does `git fetch` do?
options: Fetches and always merges changes into the current branch
Publishes local commits to the remote
Downloads remote updates and references without integrating them into the current branch
questions.correct_answer: Downloads remote updates and references without integrating them into the current branch
questions.explanation: Fetch updates remote-tracking references; you decide whether and how to merge or rebase afterward.

distractor_feedback.Fetches and always merges changes into t: `git pull` fetches and integrates according to configuration.
distractor_feedback.Deletes local commits: Fetch does not delete local commits.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is the usual effect of `git pull`
questions.question: What is the usual effect of `git pull`?
options: Fetches remote changes and integrates them into the current branch
questions.correct_answer: Fetches remote changes and integrates them into the current branch
questions.explanation: `git pull` combines fetching with integration, commonly merge or rebase depending on configuration.

distractor_feedback.Deletes the current branch: Branch deletion uses a branch deletion command.
distractor_feedback.Uploads all uncommitted files: Uncommitted files are not simply uploaded by pull.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: Which command sends local commits to a remote repository
questions.question: Which command sends local commits to a remote repository?
questions.correct_answer: git push
questions.explanation: `git push` publishes local commits to a configured remote branch.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: What is a merge conflict
questions.question: What is a merge conflict?
options: A commit message that is too short
A situation where Git cannot automatically reconcile competing changes
questions.correct_answer: A situation where Git cannot automatically reconcile competing changes
questions.explanation: Conflicts occur when changes overlap or otherwise cannot be combined automatically; a person must resolve them.

distractor_feedback.A missing Git installation: If Git is missing, Git commands cannot run.
distractor_feedback.A commit message that is too short: Commit-message length does not create a merge conflict.
distractor_feedback.A failed internet connection only: Network failure may stop remote operations but is not a merge conflict.

questions.section: M1 Week 3 — Git and Version Control
questions.topic: After resolving conflict markers in a file, what should you normally do next
questions.question: After resolving conflict markers in a file, what should you normally do next?
options: Run git clone over the current folder
Assume Git has already committed the resolution
Stage the resolved file and complete the merge commit if Git requires it
questions.correct_answer: Stage the resolved file and complete the merge commit if Git requires it
questions.explanation: After editing a conflicted file, stage it to mark it resolved, then complete the merge according to Git's instructions.

distractor_feedback.Delete the entire repository: Deleting the repository is unnecessary and destructive.
distractor_feedback.Run git clone over the current folder: Cloning is not how a merge is completed.
distractor_feedback.Assume Git has already committed the res: Git generally waits for the resolution to be staged and merge completed.

questions.section: M1 Week 4 — Bash Scripting, Automation and Cron
questions.topic: What is Bash
questions.question: What is Bash?
options: A command-line shell that can also run scripts
